content.overview: Section 45 provides that every share in a company having a share capital shall be distinguished by its distinctive number: Provided that nothing in this section shall apply to a share held by a person whose name is entered as holder of beneficial interest in such share in the records of a depository.
content.glance: Every share must have a distinctive number, except dematerialised shares held through a depository.
content.study: Every share in a company having a share capital shall be distinguished by its distinctive number. The proviso excludes shares held by a person whose name is entered as holder of beneficial interest in the records of a depository. Current-law framing: certificated shares require distinctive numbers; demat shares are excepted.

sections.heading: Distinctive number rule
sections.body: Every share in a company having a share capital shall be distinguished by its distinctive number.

sections.heading: Demat exception
sections.body: Nothing in this section applies to a share held by a person whose name is entered as holder of beneficial interest in such share in the records of a depository.

examples.title: Certificated shares
examples.body: Physical share certificates carry distinctive numbers. Section 45 is complied with.

examples.title: Demat shares
examples.body: Shares held in a demat account need not carry distinctive numbers under the proviso to s. 45.

hypotheticals.question: Must dematerialised shares be numbered?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The proviso excludes shares held with a depository where the holder is entered as beneficial owner.

misconceptions.trap: All shares, including demat, must have distinctive numbers.
misconceptions.correction: The proviso excludes dematerialised shares held through a depository.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 45 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the facts. II. Apply the statutory rule. III. Note exceptions. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Facts; statutory rule; exception if any; precise relief.

examTips: State the rule and the demat proviso.
